title: Indian Startup Funding Rebounds to $955 Million in August, Led by EV and Fintech
excerpt: Startup funding jumped 44% from July's lows, with River Mobility, Navi, and Yulu leading growth-stage deals while early-stage ventures captured 42% of total capital.
body:
• Indian startups raised approximately $955 million across 88 deals in August, a 44% jump from July's $662 million and the third-highest monthly total of 2026
  • EV led all sectors with $256 million across six deals, followed by fintech at $201 million and AI at $134 million
  • Early-stage deals contributed 42% of total funding at $400 million, with Airbound, Centricity, and InRisk Labs leading the segment
  • Bengaluru dominated with 69% of all funding, while IPO-bound startups Shiprocket, Milky Mist, and Leap debuted at a premium

Indian startup funding rebounded sharply in August, with companies raising approximately $955 million across 88 deals after a subdued July, according to data compiled by Entrackr. The total marks a 44.3% month-on-month increase from July's $662 million and represents the third-highest monthly tally of 2026, behind March ($2.09 billion) and June ($1.47 billion).

Year-on-year, however, funding was essentially flat: August 2026's $955 million was nearly identical to the $961 million raised in August 2025, even as the number of deals declined from 100 to 88.

Big Deals Drive the Recovery

Growth and late-stage funding accounted for $555 million across 13 deals. EV startup River Mobility led the month with a $120 million Series C round, followed by fintech company Navi at $100 million — its first institutional funding round, ahead of a planned IPO — and mobility startup Yulu at $93 million. AI startup Sarvam AI secured $74 million, while Third Wave Coffee, Leap India, and BlissClub also closed notable rounds.

"AI startup Sarvam AI secured $74 million, while Third Wave Coffee, Leap India, and BlissClub also closed notable rounds."

Navi, founded by Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal, raised its round from Dutch investor Prosus at a reported valuation of $1.3 billion, according to Reuters. The company is targeting a $2 billion valuation in its planned IPO.

Early Stage Holds Strong

Early-stage deals contributed $400 million, or roughly 42% of total funding — a sign that capital continues to flow into newer ventures and not just established names. Aviation startup Airbound led the segment with $37 million, followed by wealthtech platform Centricity at $30 million and fintech startup InRisk Labs at $27 million.

Series A rounds led overall deal activity with $313 million across 27 deals, accounting for about a third of total funding. Seed-stage startups raised $46 million across 25 deals.

Bengaluru's Dominance

Bengaluru remained the undisputed hub of Indian startup funding, accounting for 47 deals worth $658 million — nearly 69% of the month's total. Delhi-NCR followed at $128 million across 20 deals, with Mumbai at $83 million across eight deals.

By sector, EV emerged as the top-funded segment at $256 million across six deals, representing 26.9% of total funding. Fintech followed at $201 million, AI at $134 million, and e-commerce at $48 million.

IPOs and Exits

August also saw positive signals from the public markets. Shiprocket, Milky Mist, and Leap all made strong market debuts at a premium, according to Entrackr, despite mixed sentiment around startup IPOs more broadly.

On the other side, the month recorded 620 layoffs — 350 at healthtech startup Even Healthcare and 270 at Zomato (now Eternal). E-grocery startup Satvacart shut down operations entirely.

Where the Market Stands

The August numbers suggest that India's startup ecosystem is stabilizing after the turbulence of the past two years, with capital flowing across stages and sectors even as deal volumes compress. Aviation, spacetech, and EV attracted particularly strong interest, while the healthy share of early-stage funding indicates that new company formation remains active.

For the Indian tech diaspora — founders, engineers, and investors who straddle Silicon Valley and Bengaluru — the data points to a market that rewards both established companies with clear scale-up potential and early-stage ventures in emerging sectors like deeptech and clean mobility.
